author: Barbara Minto
title: Minto Pyramid Principle and SCQ
application: Group supporting ideas under a main point and identify the reader question through situation and complication.
limitation: A consultant framework, not an experiment showing blog performance.

author: Nancy Duarte (2010)
title: Why resonate?
application: Use narrative tension and a meaningful change when the material warrants it.
limitation: Presentation-oriented practitioner account; no universal story formula.

author: Graham Gibbs (1988); Oxford Brookes University
title: Learning by Doing / publisher publications page
application: Use reflection on experience as a thinking aid; our short scene/reflection/next-question scaffold is an adaptation.
limitation: Original PDF access returned 403; no claim to have inspected the full book or validated the six-stage model.

author: Baethge, Goldbeck-Wood, Mertens (2019)
title: SANRA—a scale for the quality assessment of narrative review articles
locator: Abstract; Methods; Discussion: validity and limitations
application: Check purpose, search description, references, reasoning, and relevant data.
limitation: Medical narrative-review setting; small sample and author-raters. This blog checklist is not a validated SANRA score.

author: Rethlefsen et al. (2021)
title: PRISMA-S
application: Retain actual sources searched, strategies, dates, restrictions and selection decisions.
limitation: Transparent search reporting is not proof that a scoped blog search is exhaustive or a systematic review.

author: Wineburg and McGrew (2019)
title: Lateral Reading and the Nature of Expertise
locator: Abstract; author research summary at cor.inquirygroup.org
application: Investigate who stands behind a source and check its claims against other evidence.
limitation: Use as a source-checking practice; do not infer that this plugin was tested in that study.

author: GO FAIR Foundation
title: FAIR principles
application: Use stable IDs, useful metadata, provenance and reuse records for evidence.
limitation: Our small JSON registers are inspired by these ideas, not FAIR certification. Original Nature article could not be fetched.

author: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative
title: Complex Images
application: Give complex visuals an equivalent text description and appropriate underlying information.
limitation: Accessibility requires actual inspection beyond a structural checker.

author: GitHub
title: Managing a custom domain for GitHub Pages
locator: Apex domain; subdomain; custom Actions note
application: Set the repository domain and correct apex and www DNS records.
limitation: DNS propagation and certificate issuance are external. With Actions, CNAME alone does not configure the domain.

author: Hugo
title: Deploy to GitHub Pages
application: Build Hugo production output and deploy that artifact through Pages Actions.
limitation: Adapted for this folder structure and explicit editorial gate; versions are pinned by us.

author: OpenAI
title: Package your plugin
locator: Local plugin install; marketplace metadata; enable for repo
application: Keep skills in a plugin, register the repo marketplace, install and verify the cached copy.
limitation: Repo discovery, installation and activation are separate states; local installs may require an app refresh.

author: Cloudflare
title: Proxy status
application: DNS-only sends traffic directly to the origin. Use it for the initial GitHub Pages setup.
limitation: The initial DNS-only choice is our deployment decision; Cloudflare generally recommends proxying web traffic.

author: OpenAI
title: Build skills
application: Use scoped skills with clear discovery metadata and supporting resources.
limitation: Skill formatting does not prove writing quality or truthfulness.
